newsitem.title: QATAR: GCC gas share to increase with new discoveries.
newsitem.headline: GCC gas share to increase with new discoveries.

text.p: More gas exploration in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states should lead to the six-member group increasing their share of the global gas market, a leading GCC energy expert said on Sunday.

"The GCC region holds at present 20.5 trillion cubic metres of gas reserves or 14.7 percent of the world total...The expectation is that it will be significantly upgraded," Anwar Yusuf Abdullah, head of the GCC's energy secretariat said.
Gas exploration was being accelerated in the GCC to meet rising domestic power and industrial demand and to supply export-orientated gas projects.

Based on the rate of recent gas discoveries in the region, Abdullah estimated that total proved reserves could rise to 28.7 trillion cubic metres or 20.5 percent of the world total in the next few years.
The GCC's role in world export markets is still limited with 1995 exports of 5.4 billion cubic metres accounting for just five percent of marketed output. The rest was consumed locally.
New liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects in Qatar and Oman and plans for cross-border pipelines should lift this figure.
The oil-rich GCC is an economic, political and military grouping of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Oman, Qatar and Bahrain.
Most GCC gas reserves are centred in Qatar, United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia.
Abdullah was speaking to a gas conference in Doha organised by the GCC and the European Commission which is looking at possible gas ties between the two groups.
